steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Miss Evie, are you heading to the front desk of the recovery ward? In that case, could you bring this little package over for me? I've got something urgent to deal with...

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Oh, Miss Evie, when you go get water, could you bring some for the little girl in the next room too? She never drinks enough water! I've told her a million times but it never gets through!

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Okay... Sure... Of course...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Wait and see how things unfold
See how many unrelated things she comes back with

choices.text: Wait and see how things unfold
See how many unrelated things she comes back with

steps.content: You trail behind Evie, watching as she picks up documents, a lunch tray, and packages along the way. The glass of water she originally went out to fetch, on the other hand, never once makes it into her hands.

No matter how many people stop her, she responds to each one with the same compliance, taking on everything as though she can't feel strain. Even as her arms grow sore, she trudges on, step by shuffling step.
She's like a dried-out tumbleweed. She always seems to be on her way somewhere, yet has no real sense of where that somewhere is. She's simply rolling whichever way each person nudges her.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Evie! Not again! Can you stop being such a pushover? That's exactly why you're taking so long to recover. Someone calls, and you just go along with whatever they say! Do you even care about your own body?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Sorry...

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: I've heard that a million times too. Has anything I've said gotten through to you at all?! Chief, you talk some sense into her too! At this rate, she's never going to be discharged!

It makes sense that nothing's getting through. Evie may not have closed off her heart, but it's hollow all the same. She's lost the only pillar she always leaned on, and that's likely the main reason she's recovering so slowly.
In reality, though, you already know where to find the cure.
Inside the vehicle

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: ...Is this the little surprise... that you said will help with my recovery?

The car turns the corner and pulls up in front of a worn-down livehouse. Evie, who had let herself be dragged into the car like a sleepwalker without a word of protest, widens her eyes ever so slightly the moment she sees it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's right. A friend of yours and I spent a good while putting this together. I hope it'll help with your recovery... and more than anything, I hope you like it.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: A friend? But I don't really have any friends...
Black Screen

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Wait?! Wh-what is this...?!
Inside the livehouse

You push open the back door. The hinges let out a soft creak. Lights come on one by one, but what they reveal is no dusty relic of the past. The moment the freshly decorated backstage comes into view, whatever words Evie had on her lips die in her throat.

The old walls are covered in panels of deep black and blue, with strings of small orange lights and cat-ear stickers tucked into the corners. It's clear that whoever designed this meant for Evie to be the center of this stage, and Mimi-meow is simply the decoration around her.

It has all the makings of a carefully planned exhibition. Draped display boards stand paired with boxes in front of them, each one a puzzle waiting to be opened alongside its answer. Evie is stunned, unsure what to say as her gaze sweeps across it all. Then, she looks back at you, as if to seek your help.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Gesture for her to explore on her own

choices.text: Gesture for her to explore on her own

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Can I really... touch any of this? That box is so big and tall... there's got to be a cake or a sculpture inside... What if I break something...
She hesitantly lifts the lid, only to find that it really is a cake inside. It looks identical to the one she never got to give away. The only difference is the writing on top: For our dear Evie.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: This is... for me? But... why would...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Who knows? Maybe someone saw the feelings you never got to express, and wanted to give something back.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: But I've ordered one before... I know how expensive this is! Who would ever want to get this for me...?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That just means they think you're worth it. Now then, why don't you cut into it and have a taste? After all, you never got to eat the last one, no?

Sure enough, there's a cake knife inside the box. Last time, amidst those blazing lights and the expectant eyes of a crowd, Evie had pushed it toward her idol. This time, however, Evie is the one who needs to decide whether to pick it up.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I didn't know... that cutting a cake like this is so difficult... Of course, I'm well aware of how expensive and special it was, but I never once thought about how hard it'd be to cut into, how hard it'd be to hold...

She struggles with every cut, her hands still too weak to apply much force. Then, as she finally works through the thick layer of frosting, she accidentally pulls the draping cloth off the display board beside her.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Are these... photos of me?

On the board are several photos, all captured from behind the scenes. One depicts Evie leaning over to adjust the lights, another depicts her solemnly flipping through the runsheet. There's also one that shows Evie looking back with a smile as she wheels out the cake, as if cradling the entire sea of orange lights in her arms.
And beside them is decorative lettering that appears to be a personal reflection—

<color=#675E8F>"I didn't understand it back then. Is this really necessary? And how is this worth it? But even when effort is pointed in the wrong direction, the sincerity behind it still warrants gratitude. So no matter how things turned out, I will always remember it, and honor it."</color>

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: So... you kept a record of all this too. Thank you, Chief. I really... don't know what to say.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is only the first one, Evie. It's a little too early for thanks. Now then, keep going.

She sets down the cake and moves toward the other display boards. This time, her steps are much quicker, much more certain than before. You walk alongside her as the photos on the boards take you back to the past, from that 365th show, all the way to even earlier days:

One Evie hand-drew signs to patch up the organizer's mistakes and was mistaken for staff. One Evie knitted wool stockings by hand for cheering on Christmas Eve. One Evie is holding a flashlight to light the way during a blackout, from before her powers awakened...

Every little thing she herself had forgotten—brushed off as "no big deal," "nothing worth mentioning"—had been carefully cleaned, arranged, and dated by someone else. Under the warm orange glow, they now lead her deeper into her own memories.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: <color=#675E8F>"Nobody knew you could draw until that day. Just how many surprises are you hiding?" "The colors might be off, but this has to be the best stocking anyone could ever receive as a gift." "Your lighting work was actually better back then."</color>...

Through the back door, down the corridor, past the wings, across the stage, and into the audience seats. Evie walks through the live house from the back to the front, not wanting to miss a single display board, losing her breath more than once along the way.

Finally, she stops before the last box and display board, set up right at the main entrance of the venue. She turns to look at you with tears in her eyes, the doubt and confusion that once tainted her voice now gone.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: ...You weren't the one who actually prepared these, were you, Chief?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: There's so much here that you... or even the others in Mimi-meow's fandom... couldn't possibly know about... I didn't even know anyone still remembered any of this...
You only smile. Evie doesn't press for your confirmation either, and simply turns around to open the box behind her.

Sure enough, inside is a blurry photo taken from the stage. In it, Evie is plainly dressed and in an absolute mess of tears. Meanwhile, Mimi-meow is beside her with an expression that is equal parts awkward and inexperienced. This is from that very first live show. Their first meeting.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: <color=#675E8F>"You always tell everyone you'll never forget how radiant I was at that show. But if anything, I'm the one who'll never forget—it was the look on your face that convinced me so."</color>

Evie reads the words on the display board, choking and sobbing all the while. As for who prepared all this, the answer is clear as day to her now—it's Mimi-meow. It's her who set all this up, who cropped every photo to put Evie at the center.

Light, it turns out, was never a one-sided thing. She had always believed she was simply lucky enough to be illuminated by that sun, never knowing that her every response was what fueled that brilliance.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Mimi-meow... it was you, wasn't it? You actually remembered all these little things...

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: There must have been a reason you said those things back then! I won't misunderstand you again, so... please come out!
Evie wipes her tears with the back of her hand, her gaze sweeping the room without direction. Her voice grows urgent, still a little nasal from crying, and barely able to contain her anticipation.
It echoes through the empty live house for a moment, yet no one answers. You watch as Evie stands there, a little lost, and step forward to give her one last hint.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hold on, take a look outside the door. Maybe Mimi-meow hasn't shown up yet... because you haven't finished the route?
Outdoor Clearing

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: There's... one last box? But... the debut live is as far back as I can remember... Don't tell me... D-did I forget something Mimi-meow considers important...?! I-I'm a failure as a fan!

She pushes open the door to find a path decorated with paper blossoms, gold and silver ribbons, and hand-drawn stickers. At the far end, atop a makeshift stage, sits the last box. Evie approaches it, confused and nervous. Yet, inside is nothing but an old flyer.
The flyer is yellowed and poorly printed. On it is a Mimi-meow with a very forced smile, her poses exaggerated. She looks brand new and unpolished, like something fresh out of the packaging.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: This... I had one of these too. I kept it tucked in my files, but when I got a new bag... I lost it. I felt awful about it for a while. But... what does this mean?

She thinks for a long while, but the answer still eludes her. Figures. You lightly shake your head, press the button hidden behind your back, and the lights around blaze to life at once. This was the signal you arranged with your special guest.

In the next instant, the gold and silver ribbons catch the light and shatter into countless glittering sparks, as the idol whose name has been called so many times makes her grand entrance from the far end of the path.

The moment she sees Mimi-meow, Evie drops her gaze, almost unable to look directly at her. She becomes rooted to the spot, too overcome to take a single step forward. She only manages to wave her hands frantically, stumbling over her words as she tries to express just how moved she is.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I'm sorry, I never should have doubted you. I always knew you were the best idol in the world... Thank you for all of this. I'll never question whether you truly care about your fans again. No matter what happens from here, I'll support you for the rest of my——

The crisp click of heels cuts her off and makes her look up. Her idol had been standing at the far end of that light just a moment ago, looking exactly as she did the first time Evie ever saw her, when she lit up Evie's world.

But now, she walks toward her, draped in light and crowned in stars. It's as if she's stepping out from that old flyer, those display boards, those treasured memories... She closes the distance between them one step at a time, until they've finally come face-to-face. She opens her mouth with a smile.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: I'm the one who should be thanking you, Evie. Thank you for being willing to give me another chance, even after hearing those hurtful words. Thank you for making it all the way here.
Mimi-meow reaches out and takes Evie's restless hands. She pauses, then shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: But... I'm sorry. I can't accept those compliments. Because today, I'm not standing here as an idol.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: ...Not as an idol? What does that mean? It's just like last time, when you said you "don't need our love"... I know you probably meant no harm, and maybe you were just looking out for me, but... it just confuses me even more.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Did I do something wrong... as a fan? Or have you given up on the idol industry, and you don't want to be an <color=#fb9259>idol</color> anymore? Is it that you don't want to be my <color=#fb9259>light</color> anymore?!

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: No, of course not, Evie. Please, calm down. I've always felt genuinely proud that my work can bring happiness to people. Because even if that happiness is fleeting, even if it's not entirely real, I know you care. Someone cares.

Mimi-meow takes Evie's hand, gentle and reassuring, then turns to lead her toward the path stretching behind them. The display boards and old objects they passed along the way rest quietly, like a still and luminous river.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Seeing the darker side of the idol industry won't make me deny the hope it's given you. The reason I stepped onto that stage in the first place was to offer a little warmth and light for people like you.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Then why... why did you turn me down like that? You saved me, so I wanted to repay the favor, to help more people see you... That's how I show love. That's how any fan shows love.
Evie's voice is trembling, barely above a whisper. The pain of being wholly dismissed rises in her again, and still she has no answer.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Is there something I could've done better? Something you didn't like? But you remembered everything I did, you kept all of it... Isn't this whole path proof of that? So why do you make it sound like none of it was enough?

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: It's not that there's something I don't like, Evie. I just can't accept you hurting yourself for my sake.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Yes, it's natural to want to do something for someone you care about. And I've always treasured everything you've done for me. But if the price of that <color=#fb9259>love</color> means you need to cough until you can barely stand, to smile and say you're fine when you're completely exhausted...

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Then I don't want <color=#fb9259>it</color>, nor can I afford it.
Evie looks down at her hand, held in Mimi-meow's. That same hand that has done so much for others now sits there, uncertain what to do with itself, simply because someone is holding it with care.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: But... I really don't know what else I can do. If I'm not out there doing something for you, what right do I have to be <color=#fb9259>illuminated</color> by you?
This time, she doesn't say sorry. The genuine confusion she has always kept tucked behind those "I'm fine" and "I can do it" finally finds its voice here.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: The fledgling underground idol back then was no different from any other girl in Eastside with her head in the clouds. If we're talking about "rights," what right did she have to be chosen by you, to be saved by you?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: What... do you mean...?
Seeing that Evie hasn't understood at all, Mimi-meow can't help but chuckle. She takes a step back and lifts the cloth covering the last display board with her free hand.
On it is a photograph of the Eastside nightscape, entirely unremarkable.
Eastside Nightscape, Flashback

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Hello there! I'm an underground idol making my debut tonight. My name is Mimi-meow. The show is free, would you like to come and give it a listen?

Showtime draws closer and closer, yet the unknown underground idol is still out on the street with a promotional flag strapped to her back, handing out flyers. If the audience count doesn't meet the minimum her agency set, it's back to the gutter for her.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Hello! Long day at work? How about a song to lift your spirits? I'll give it everything I've got out there, so come on down to my free debut show!
Sorry, but I'm in a rush to get home...
No luck again. The weary office workers shuffling past are always equal parts hollow and hurried, so the fact that this girl even bothered to respond is, if anything, a courtesy.

Mimi-meow has already given up. She carefully presses the back of her hand to the corner of her eye, not wanting to smudge her makeup, then puts on a smile again and turns to face the next disappointment. Yet, the office worker before her catches the glimmer at the edge of her eye, and suddenly comes to a stop.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Wait, hold on. Is that you on this flyer? You're so cute! Can I have one...? You said the show is free, right? Do I just need to bring the flyer to get in?

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: ...! Yes! The flyer is your ticket! A-and you'll get a custom orange glow stick too! You'll really feel like part of the show, so please, do come watch!

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Oh, but the venue looks a little hard to find, and I'm not sure where it is exactly... The show's starting pretty soon, right? I can wait here while you finish handing out flyers. Could you walk me there?

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Of course! I'll lead the way!

Their exchange draws the attention of a few passersby. Some of them had been eyeing the address on the promotional flag with skepticism. After hearing the back-and-forth, they hesitantly step up, forming a short little tail of a line.

steps.speaker: Passerby A
steps.content: It's not too far off anyway. Might as well check it out if someone's leading the way.

steps.speaker: Passerby B
steps.content: Huh? Why's there a line over there? Maybe I'll go take a look.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Hello! Hello! Yes, it's my debut show tonight! I'm Mimi-meow, an <color=#fb9259>underground idol</color> who's here to bring everyone <color=#fb9259>love</color>, hope, and the scent of oranges! Care to come take a listen?
Outdoor Clearing

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: If it weren't for you, I never could have filled the quota my agency set. I wouldn't be standing here today. And yet, whenever you tell the story of how we met, you always leave that part out.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: It was never me who started it all. It was you. Before I ever <color=#fb9259>"saved"</color> you, before I ever <color=#fb9259>"illuminated"</color> you, you had already saved me. You're the one who changed my fate, Miss Softhearted.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: So you see, Evie, you don't need to push yourself to your limits or endure the pain to do something worthwhile. You already managed to <color=#fb9259>illuminate</color> me that night, just like the neon lights of Eastside.
Evie's face goes blank. She murmurs.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I completely forgot that even happened... It really was just a coincidence... M-Mimi-meow, did you cry back then? I don't remember anymore...

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: That's okay. Because it only proves that simply following your heart and doing what you truly want to do is enough to obtain <color=#fb9259>love</color>. You've proven it yourself, no?
Mimi-meow steps aside and guides Evie to the center of the stage. She watches Evie, bathed in light, with satisfaction. The tears she had held back behind her glittery stage makeup finally fall.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: And that's exactly why I don't want the agency to deceive you, exploit you, use you for your commercial value, or make you hurt yourself in the process.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: That's why I told Chief I wanted to give you an exhibition with you as the star, a stage where you stand at the center.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: I wanted you to know that a fan doesn't need to use herself as <color=#fb9259>kindling</color> to <color=#fb9259>illuminate</color> an idol. From the very beginning, it should have been two lights reflecting off each other. The light you gave me was never supposed to come at the cost of extinguishing your own.

Evie's eyes begin to tear up. Not because she feels wounded from being scolded, nor is it because of some delirious joy from being praised by her idol. Those tears come from something that has long taken root deep inside her, a seedling that has finally found sunlight and rain, now breaking through the clouds in her chest.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: C-can I... really still be <color=#fb9259>loved</color>, even without doing all those things? Can I really obtain <color=#fb9259>love</color> for myself... without putting in so much more effort than everyone else?
Mimi-meow lifts their still-joined hands, gestures down the path she walked in from, then up toward the lights above. She asks, beaming—

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Evie, am I brilliant?
Evie says nothing, and simply nods.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: You were the one who gave this path and light to me. So, if you think it's brilliant...
She pauses, her voice dropping, somewhere between a plea and a prayer.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Then please, love the you who gave me that light. Love the you that I love.

Evie is too moved to speak, but her hand reaches out without a moment's hesitation to wipe the tears from the corner of Mimi-meow's eyes. She keeps wiping until the redness fades and the tears stop falling. Only then does she turn to brush her own face dry.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Thank you, Mimi-meow, thank you for doing so much for me... I'll try! I-I don't know if I can manage it right away, but I'll try...
Watching the scene before you, you finally can't help but break into a warm round of applause.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Ch-Chief...! Th-thank you too... Mimi-meow couldn't have arranged all of this on her own, right...? Otherwise, she would have done it long ago...

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I've caused you so much trouble already, and you still came with me to the concert, helped me keep my Mania in check, and on top of all that, you went out of your way to do all this for me... I-I really don't know how I could ever repay you...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I thought we're past the whole repaying thing now?

choices.text: I thought we're past the whole repaying thing now?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well, Mimi-meow and I didn't plan all of this to tell you that caring for others and giving of yourself is wrong, anyway. We just want you to value yourself more, and to recognize your own worth.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And I hope you'll stop draining yourself. Don't push your special power past its limits for the kind of love that comes wrapped in pretty words and a price tag anymore. Don't destabilize your M-value for such things.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for the agency inducing a Sinner to participate in commercial promotions and using powers in violation of regulations, you can leave them to the Bureau. That is not a responsibility you need to shoulder on anyone else's behalf.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I'll keep that in mind...
Evie, convinced she's been nothing but a burden, flushes red and nods. She stumbles over her words, caught somewhere between an apology and a thank-you. You stop her before she can get either out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't give us too much credit. There's a saying among Eastia's Sinners—let he who tied the bell on the tiger take it off. If you hadn't already laid the groundwork, Mimi-meow and I would have had nothing to build on. You were always the one who saved yourself.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: ${PlayerName} is right, Evie. I don't want you putting yourself below me all the time, always thinking about how to repay me. All you really need to do is come to my shows as a fan, and just enjoy them.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: ...Okay!
Mimi-meow lets out a sigh of relief at the rare certainty in that answer. Finally, a familiar smile breaks through. That expression is bright and warm, one that belongs to an idol.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: That's wonderful! Now that Evie's trip down memory lane has come to a perfect close, it's time for the encore! Just sit back and enjoy this last song. I'm dedicating it to you!
Evie goes red from her face all the way down to her neck, both surprised and delighted. You smile, pull out a speaker, and start the music. Apparently, it's a cover Mimi-meow sang at her debut show.

As the melody begins, Evie tries to step off the stage, but Mimi-meow catches her hand and refuses to let go. So, she stays. At first she's stiff as a rock, but by the time the chorus rolls around, that awkwardness has all but dissipated, and she's clapping along and singing under her breath.

Just then, the lights above the stage flicker twice. The makeshift wiring pulled from the near-derelict building has finally been pushed past its limit. A couple of the old fixtures crackle, and then go dark.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Oh, the lights...!
Half of Mimi-meow's figure is swallowed by the darkness. Almost by instinct, Evie's Mania stirs, and a familiar flicker of orange light rises to her fingertips.
You don't rush to activate your shackles. You simply watch as she closes her own hand first, letting that small light flicker softly in her palm, then fade.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: No, wait... I made a promise to Mimi-meow and Chief. I need to think of another way...

She turns and unclips a string of decorative lights from the edge of the flower path. Since they were powered by batteries, they still work fine, though the plastic casing is rough to the touch and the light they give off is faint. Even with several strung together, they couldn't hope to light a whole stage.

But that's alright. She wraps the lights around her and Mimi-meow's joined hands, then lifts them up to Mimi-meow's face. The warm glow catches the little idol's smile, still as bright and lovely as ever.
It's the first time she's learned to answer Mimi-meow with her own light, however small. And there, in the dim glow, you feel that Mimi-meow is smiling too.
Chief's Office.
A few days later, on an ordinary weekday lunch break, your terminal lights up with a string of notifications. You open it to find a few messages from Evie.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: Sorry to bother you, Chief. The results from my last check-up at the Bureau came back, and I've been cleared to return to normal life.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: You might already know this, but I wanted to personally let you know anyway, since you've done so much for me.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: That's great to hear. But... no staying up late, no excessive caffeine, no standing for too long... That's quite a few restrictions. Will you really be able to stick to all these?

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: Mimi-meow said she'll be keeping an eye on me, and the punishment for going back on my word is terrifying, so... Definitely! [Scared face emoji]

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Please elaborate.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: [image]

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: We spotted this pair of little figurines at a boutique in Eastside the other day, and the color scheme looked just like me and Mimi-meow!

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: She bought the orange-yellow one for me, and I bought the blue-black one for her. She said if I can't keep it together, she'll take my Mimi-meow away.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: I can't afford to lose custody, so...

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Sounds like it's very effective. This plan has my full support.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Neither of them insisted on paying for both. A good sign, if I may say so myself.
You close the chat with a smile, and as you do, your eyes catch Evie's profile status. It reads: "I'm free!!!!"
